text:
Aisha: hey team, i'm wrapping up my first feature PR and want to double-check our codebase/PR norms. quick checklist? especially around branch naming, PR size, and automated labels.
Marcus: welcome! short checklist: branch off main, keep PRs under ~400 changed lines if possible, include tests, run local lint/tests, and add a short testing section in the PR description.
Riley: branch names: feature/<ticket>-short-desc for features, fix/<ticket>-short for bugfixes, chore/<area>/short for chores. ticket is optional if none. e.g., feature/1234-add-cache.
Aisha: ok about commit style: do you prefer many small commits or one squashed commit?
Marcus: prefer tidy history. Use multiple commits during development if helpful, but squash to a coherent single commit per logical change before merge unless reviewers ask to keep history. Use imperative subject lines.
Riley: commit message examples:
- "feat(cache): add per-user response cache"
- "fix(api): handle 502 from upstream"
Also include a short body if there is non-obvious rationale.
doc-bot: style-guide: https://redwood.internal/dev/conventions — includes commit/PR examples, labeling rules, and CODEOWNERS behavior.
Aisha: labels — do I add them or CI adds them?
Marcus: CI auto-applies size/* based on diff. You should add type labels (feat, fix, chore) and any owner/team labels (e.g., infra, runtime) before requesting review.
Riley: reviewers: request 1 reviewer for internal-only changes, 2 for infra/runtime or public API changes. If CODEOWNERS lists required reviewers they'll be added automatically, but ping someone directly for faster turnaround.
Aisha: anything specific about tests? unit + small integration? snapshot policy?
Marcus: unit tests are required for logic changes. Integration tests for feature flows that touch multiple services. Avoid huge e2e in PRs; prefer a small smoke test and a follow-up e2e in CI. Snapshots ok for UI-ish outputs but prefer explicit assertions where possible.
Riley: checking CI: expect lint, unit, build-image, and a lightweight integration on main. If you touch proto files or public schemas, add a compatibility note in PR and tag "api-compat".
ci-bot: CI queued for feature/1234-add-cache  lint/checks pending.
Aisha: last Q  what's our approach to migration or feature flags?
Marcus: prefer feature flags for anything behind rollout. include a cleanup task in the PR description if you add a flag. For DB migrations: small, additive-first migrations only; coordinate with infra if it affects large tables.
Riley: tiny nit: PR titles should be imperative and capitalized e.g., "Add per-user response cache". In PR body include: summary, test steps, rollout plan, and any owners.
Aisha: perfect thanks — i'll update the PR template and ping Marcus for review. :)
Marcus: welcome aboard! ping if you want a 15-min walkthrough of the repo layout. :wave:
